Build, write, run, and read RSA models for Mplus

Source: R/rsa-mplus-workflow.R
create_rsa_mplus_model.Rd

These functions provide a composable workflow for response surface models estimated in Mplus. create_rsa_mplus_model() uses tidySEM for ordinary measurement and structural paths, then adds the XWITH interactions and response-surface constraints required for latent polynomial models.

Usage

create_rsa_mplus_model(
  data,
  measurement,
  structural = NULL,
  roles = c(x = "X", y = "Y", outcome = "Z"),
  model_type = c("latent", "si_lms"),
  reliability = NULL,
  constraints = c("surface", "principal"),
  blocks = list(),
  model_extra = NULL,
  constraint_extra = NULL,
  usevariables = NULL,
  identification = c("marker", "effects", "invariance"),
  center = c("none", "pooled"),
  free_intercepts = NULL,
  rsa_model = "full",
  start = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE
)

write_rsa_mplus_model(
  x,
  modelout,
  dataout = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

run_rsa_mplus_model(
  x,
  Mplus_command = NULL,
  replace_outfile = c("always", "never", "modifiedDate"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

read_rsa_mplus_model(target, output = NULL, quiet = TRUE)

rsa_mplus_workflow(
  data,
  measurement,
  structural = NULL,
  roles = c(x = "X", y = "Y", outcome = "Z"),
  model_type = c("latent", "si_lms"),
  reliability = NULL,
  constraints = c("surface", "principal"),
  blocks = list(),
  model_extra = NULL,
  constraint_extra = NULL,
  usevariables = NULL,
  identification = c("marker", "effects", "invariance"),
  center = c("none", "pooled"),
  free_intercepts = NULL,
  rsa_model = "full",
  start = NULL,
  modelout,
  dataout = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  run = FALSE,
  Mplus_command = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing all variables exported to Mplus.

measurement

A named list mapping latent variables to indicators, or a character vector of lavaan/tidySEM measurement statements.

structural

Optional structural model. Supply a named list mapping outcomes to predictors, or a character vector of lavaan/tidySEM paths. The core X and Y paths to the RSA outcome are added when absent.

roles

Named character vector with elements x, y, and outcome identifying the latent variables used in the RSA model.

model_type

Either "latent" for multi-indicator factors or "si_lms" for reliability-corrected single-indicator factors.

reliability

For model_type = "si_lms", a named numeric vector of reliability estimates for the three latent variables in roles.

constraints

Which built-in constraints to include. "surface" produces cs, cc, is, ic, and a5; "principal" additionally produces the stationary point and principal axes for the models that have them (see Details).

blocks

Named list of Mplus input blocks. Values replace defaults for the corresponding block. MODEL and MODELCONSTRAINT are reserved; use model_extra and constraint_extra to extend them. The VARIABLE block may contain additional directives, but USEVARIABLES is generated from usevariables and must not be supplied through blocks.

model_extra

Additional raw statements appended to the Mplus MODEL block.

constraint_extra

Additional raw statements appended to the Mplus MODEL CONSTRAINT block.

usevariables

Character vector of data columns to export and include in the Mplus USEVARIABLES statement. Defaults to all columns in data.

identification

How the X, Y, and outcome factors are scaled, for model_type = "latent". "marker" (default) fixes the first loading of each factor to 1. "effects" uses effects coding (Little, Slegers, & Card, 2006): loadings are constrained to average 1, so each factor is on the metric of its average indicator. This changes the units of b1-b5 slightly but not the fit of the model. "invariance" keeps the marker loadings and puts the X and Y factors on one metric through scalar measurement invariance: the k-th X and Y indicators share their loading and their intercept, the two marker intercepts are fixed at 0, and both factor means are freed. It requires as many X as Y indicators, given in matching order. Unlike "effects", it restricts the model, and it writes no MODEL CONSTRAINT statements for the measurement model, so it also runs under ESTIMATOR = BAYES. See Details.

center

Origin of the X/Y plane. "none" (default) fixes both factor means at 0, so each factor is centred at its own mean and the line X = Y means "both at their average" rather than equality. "pooled", which requires identification = "effects" or "invariance", subtracts one constant (the mean of the X and Y scale means) from every X and Y indicator in a DEFINE statement and frees the two factor means; under effects coding it also constrains the intercepts to sum to zero. X = Y is then equality on the shared response scale, the latent counterpart of RSA::RSA(center = "pooled"). This assumes the X and Y items share a response metric. The move is a translation by the latent mean difference Delta = E(X) - E(Y): b3-b5, a2, a4, and a5 are unchanged, while a3 shifts by -Delta * a4 and a1 by -Delta * a5. User DEFINE statements are placed after the shift.

free_intercepts

For identification = "invariance", names of indicators whose intercept is not shared between X and Y (partial scalar invariance). Naming either member of a matched pair frees the pair. The marker pair cannot be freed.

rsa_model

Response surface model to generate, named as in the model family of the RSA package. "full" (the default) estimates all five polynomial terms. The restricted models are "SRRR", "SRR", "RR", "SRSQD", "SSQD", "SQD", "IA", "additive", "mean", "diff", "onlyx", "onlyy", "onlyx2", "onlyy2", and "null". Four further models are not part of the RSA package: "addx2", "addy2", "noIA", and "a5zero". See Details. fit_rsa_mplus_family() fits several of them from one specification.

start

Optional start values for the polynomial terms, typically the estimates of the full model. Supply a named numeric vector with names b1 to b5 (or x, y, x2, xy, and y2), a result of RSA_mplus(), or a fitted workflow. Only the terms that rsa_model estimates freely receive a start value.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress status messages from MplusAutomation.

x

An rsa_mplus_workflow object.

modelout

Path to the Mplus .inp file to create. Mplus lower-cases file names, so on a case-sensitive file system (Linux, WSL) the file name must be lower case for Mplus to find it.

dataout

Path to the Mplus data file. By default, it uses the same stem as modelout with a .dat extension.

overwrite

If TRUE, replace existing input and data files.

Mplus_command

Optional path or command used to invoke Mplus.

replace_outfile

Passed to MplusAutomation::runModels().

target

An rsa_mplus_workflow, Mplus .inp or .out path, an mplus.model, or an mplusObject containing parsed results.

output

Optional Mplus .out path to read into an existing workflow. This is useful for attaching a cached or relocated output while retaining the workflow's role metadata. It can only be used when target is an rsa_mplus_workflow.

run

If TRUE, run and read the generated Mplus model after writing its files. The default only writes reproducible input and data files.

Value

An object of class rsa_mplus_workflow. The object is updated and returned by the write, run, and read functions. Under pooled centering, spec$centering holds the subtracted constant and the two scale means it was computed from. Under invariance identification, spec$invariance holds the matched indicators and the freed pairs. spec$rsa_model names the generated model and spec$start holds the start values that were used.

Details

rsa_model writes the restrictions of the second-order models in RSA::RSA() (Schönbrodt, Testing fit patterns with polynomial regression models) on the regression weights b1 to b5. Terms set to zero are fixed with @0. The other restrictions are placed in MODEL CONSTRAINT, together with the NEW parameters that describe the restricted surface:

rsa_modelRestrictionsModel-specific NEW parameters
"full"nonex0, y0, p10, p11, p20, p21 (with "principal")
"SRRR"b3 = b4*b4/(4*b5)c, s, bm, a4r
"SRR"b3 = b5, b4 = -2*b5c, bm
"RR"b1 = b2, b3 = b5, b4 = -2*b5bm
"SRSQD"b1 = b2*b4/(2*b5), b3 = b4*b4/(4*b5)c, s, a4r
"SSQD"b1 = -b2, b3 = b5, b4 = -2*b5c
"SQD"b1 = b2 = 0, b3 = b5, b4 = -2*b5none
"IA"b3 = b5 = 0x0, y0 (with "principal")
"additive"b3 = b4 = b5 = 0none
"mean", "diff"b3 = b4 = b5 = 0, and b1 = b2 or b1 = -b2none
"onlyx2", "onlyy2"b2 = b4 = b5 = 0 or b1 = b3 = b4 = 0none
"onlyx", "onlyy"all terms but b1 or b2 are 0none
"null"all five terms are 0none
"addx2", "addy2"b4 = b5 = 0 or b3 = b4 = 0none
"noIA"b4 = 0none
"a5zero"b3 = b5none

The last four models are additions to the family of RSA::RSA(). "addx2" and "addy2" add one squared term to the plane; unlike "onlyx2" and "onlyy2", they keep both linear terms. "noIA" keeps both squared terms and drops the product. "a5zero" sets the two squared terms equal, so that a5 = 0; it is the smallest model that nests both "SRR" and "IA", which makes it a reference model for testing either of them (see reference in compare_rsa_mplus_models()).

The ridge parameters correspond to those of RSA::RSA(): c is the lateral shift C of the ridge in units of X, s the scaling S of X that rotates the ridge, bm the effect of the mean level along the ridge (meaneffect), and a4r the curvature across the rotated ridge (a4.rescaled, a4'). Each is written in its simplest closed form in b1 to b5; for example, a4' is 4*b5. The rotated models "SRRR" and "SRSQD" express b3 (and b1) as functions of the other weights. One run therefore covers both ridges and troughs, where RSA::RSA() fits an inequality-constrained model twice. These models are not defined at b5 = 0: a flat-ridge model that does not fit the data can drift towards b5 = 0 with a large c.

Surface parameters (cs, cc, is, ic, a5) that a model fixes at zero are not generated, and the others omit the terms fixed with @0, because Mplus cannot refer to such a term in MODEL CONSTRAINT. With "principal", the full model gets its stationary point and principal axes and "IA" its stationary point; the principal axes of "IA" have slopes of 1 and -1 by construction, and the other models have no stationary point. Restricted models keep the XWITH products, with fixed weights where needed, so all models are nested in the full model and their log-likelihoods can be compared. The "weak" and "strong" fit patterns of RSA::RSA() are not generated.

With identification = "invariance", the latent line X = Y is equality on the response scale because matched items measure X and Y with the same loadings and intercepts. This is an assumption about the items: it holds only if the X and Y items are parallel in wording and response format, and it can be tested with fit_rsa_mplus_invariance(). Each factor mean is then the mean of its marker item. With center = "none", the origin X = Y = 0 is the value 0 of the response scale, which usually lies outside the data; center = "pooled" moves it to the mean of the two scale means. To centre elsewhere, for example at the scale midpoint, use center = "none" and subtract that value from the X and Y indicators in blocks$DEFINE. The outcome factor keeps its marker identification.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
latent_model <- create_rsa_mplus_model(
  data = dat,
  measurement = list(
    X = c("x1", "x2", "x3"),
    Y = c("y1", "y2", "y3"),
    Z = c("z1", "z2", "z3")
  ),
  structural = list(Z = c("X", "Y"))
)
} # }
